newsitem.title: FRANCE: Truckers' strike disrupts Peugeot car production.
newsitem.headline: Truckers' strike disrupts Peugeot car production.

text.p: A four-day truckers' strike has disrupted production at PSA Peugeot Citroen's Peugeot car division, prompting the company to set short-time working at several plants, a spokesman said on Thursday.
Officials at Citroen, the other PSA division, were not immediately available for comment. Renault SA said its production was not affected by the strike.

Shifts have been reduced at Peugeot's Sochaux and Poissy plants in France, its plant in Madrid, and its Ryton plant in Britain, the Peugeot spokesman said. He said the plants were running low on parts.
Short-time working was set today at the Sochaux plant, which produces 406 and 605 models. It had been previously scheduled for short-time working on Friday.

Short-time working is set at the Poissy plant for today and Friday, the spokesman said. Previously scheduled plans for short-time working at the plant on Monday will be probably be cancelled as a result, he said.
Short-time working is set today for Ryton and was set yesterday at the Madrid plant.
The truckers' unions have called for strikes and road blockages to force the government to put pressure on employers to make concessions on wages, retirement terms and working hours.
